run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T05:40:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is explained by a short, severe burst of checkout failures on 2026-11-17 between ~05:32 and ~05:37, not by a persistent fault in frontend-proxy itself. frontend-proxy's own spans show errors on both 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' only during that interval, and its access log records 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' from 05:32:20. In the same window checkout recorded error spans on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and on its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, and the frontend recorded errors on POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder. The deepest evidence points to the payment workload: Deployment otel-demo/payment was deliberately restarted at 05:30:54 (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, generation 2), which scaled the only replica out (old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 killed 05:30:57) and started payment-54499f9786-4r25d, whose application only logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 05:32:12 and first received a charge at 05:32:45. Because the pod template has no readinessProbe, traffic was routed to the replacement before it was listening, so checkout's Charge calls failed, the frontend returned 500 on /api/checkout and frontend-proxy recorded the error spans that raised the alert. All other otel-demo workloads were untouched (no restarts, 21/21 pods Running) and the error ratio returned to background levels after 05:38. Two things could not be resolved: the RequestErrorRate rule itself is not readable in this Prometheus, and the reason for the payment rollout restart / the value of fault-injection flags at incident time cannot be established without change history.

claims.text: In the 24h to 05:57:01 frontend-proxy recorded 89.2 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation 'ingress' and 69.9 on 'router frontend egress', against 26,232 and 26,248 spans carrying STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no status, which is not a success).

The frontend-proxy error burst is confined to ~05:32-05:37: the ratio of frontend-proxy error-span rate to 'ingress' span rate was <=0.0018 before 05:32:01, rose to 0.0173 (05:32:01), 0.0411 (05:33:01), 0.0406 (05:34:01), 0.0402 (05:35:01), 0.0403 (05:36:01) and 0.0240 (05:37:01), then fell to 0.0006 at 05:38:01 and stayed <=0.0015 through 05:50:01 and 0 at 05:51:01; error spans on 'router frontend egress' are non-zero in the same 05:32-05:37 interval only.

frontend-proxy's access log records upstream 500s on the checkout route starting 05:32:20: 69 lines matching 'api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 50' between 05:30 and 05:38, shown as 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream', so these failures originate upstream (frontend) and are not generated by the proxy.

In the 05:25-05:55 error-span breakdown the frontend-proxy errors appear together with errors from its callers/callees: frontend POST /api/checkout 70.80, frontend POST 70.80 and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 70.80; checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.41 and checkout client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 42.46 errors against 792.93 UNSET charge spans.

checkout's Charge error spans are concentrated in one minute: increase over a 60s range is 82 at 05:33:01 and 0 for every point 05:34:01-05:45:01; the 5m-rate series is non-zero only in the 05:35:01 bucket (0.1595/s) and is 0 in the 05:40:01, 05:45:01 and 05:50:01 buckets.

Deployment otel-demo/payment carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:30:54Z with generation 2; its events show 'Scaled up replica set payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1' at 05:30:54, 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0' at 05:30:57, old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 'Killing' at 05:30:57 and new pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 05:30:54-05:30:57. Both ReplicaSets run the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.
Only two otel-demo deployments carry a restart annotation: payment at 2026-11-17T05:30:54Z and flagd at 2026-11-17T05:00:36Z; the other 19 deployments are generation 1 with no restartedAt.

The replacement payment container Started at 05:30:57 but its application logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 05:32:12.571; the first 'Charge request received' is 05:32:45.971, and 'Charge request received'/'Transaction complete' pairs continue through 05:44:51.957.

Payment's own server-side 'charge' span rate dropped to 0.0667/s at 05:33:01 and 0/s at 05:34:01 (from ~0.8-0.9/s) and recovered to 0.75/s at 05:35:01, while payment's own spans carried no error status (GET, dns.lookup and tcp.connect error counts are 0).

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running; checkout (checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp), frontend (frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt) and frontend-proxy (frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks) started 04:58:42-04:58:43 with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and payment-54499f9786-4r25d started 05:30:54 with restartCount 0 and empty lastState.
The payment Deployment's pod template defines no readinessProbe and sets resources limits cpu=20m, memory=160Mi and requests cpu=10m, memory=80Mi for image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap currently declares flag 'paymentUnreachable' with defaultVariant 'on' and description 'Payment service is unavailable', while every other injected-fault flag (paymentFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is 'off'.

The frontend-proxy error rate was raised by this chain: Deployment otel-demo/payment was rolled/restarted at 05:30:54, removing the only payment replica (old pod killed 05:30:57) and replacing it with a pod whose gRPC server bound only at 05:32:12; with no readinessProbe the Service endpoint accepted traffic immediately, so checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls errored (82 error spans in 05:32:01-05:33:01), the frontend returned 500 on /api/checkout (first logged 05:32:20) and frontend-proxy recorded ingress and router-egress error spans until ~05:37. The causation is inferred from matching timing and span names; the failing traces themselves are not in Jaeger.

The 20m CPU limit on the payment container (with a 10m request) plausibly stretched payment's startup so the gRPC server needed 75 s after container start to bind; no CPU-throttling or container resource metric was found to verify this.

The currently configured fault flag 'paymentUnreachable'='on' in otel-demo/flagd-config declares the same symptom (payment service unavailable) and may have been intended as the injected fault, but its value at 05:30 and any link to the payment rollout restart at 05:30:54 cannot be verified because the ConfigMap reflects only current state and change history is not integrated.

The flag 'paymentUnreachable'='on' does not match a sustained payment outage: payment completed charges successfully ('Charge request received'/'Transaction complete') from 05:32:45 through 05:44:51 and checkout's Charge error rate was 0 in every minute after 05:34:01 and in the 05:40:01/05:45:01/05:50:01 buckets, while the ConfigMap still shows the flag 'on'.

Payment's application was not returning errors: payment's own spans carry no STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and its logs show charges being completed ('Transaction complete') around the error window; the failure was therefore at call/reachability level, not payment application error handling.

The frontend tier itself was not restarted or replaced during the window: checkout, frontend and frontend-proxy pods all started 04:58:42-04:58:43 with 0 restarts and empty lastState, so their error spans were not caused by a restart of those workloads.

The flagd EventStream 'error' spans for ad (2.052), fraud-detection (2.052) and recommendation (2.052) are practically identical in the two adjacent aggregation points, indicating steady background rather than a change tied to this failure; they are also unrelated to the checkout/payment path.

Add a readinessProbe (or startupProbe) on port 8080 to the payment container and/or raise its 20m CPU limit, so the Service endpoints only include the pod after the gRPC server is listening; this removes the traffic-to-a-not-yet-listening pod gap seen at 05:30:57-05:32:12.
Run payment with more than one replica or a rolling strategy that does not drop to zero available replicas, so a single-replica restart cannot make checkout's Charge calls fail.

Review the otel-demo/flagd-config fault flags - in particular 'paymentUnreachable' left at 'on' while all other fault flags are 'off' - and confirm whether any experiment intended to leave payment marked unreachable.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition and Alertmanager state (the rule query was not readable in this Prometheus) to confirm its evaluation window and reconcile the reported current value 0.0222 with the recovered error ratio after 05:38.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data both for rule_name='RequestErrorRate' and unfiltered, so the exact expression, threshold, evaluation window and current firing state are unverified.

Change history is not an integrated data source, so who/why issued the payment rollout restart (restartedAt 2026-11-17T05:30:54Z) and the flagd restart (restartedAt 2026-11-17T05:00:36Z), and whether otel-demo/flagd-config changed then, cannot be determined; the ConfigMap is only its current state.

Jaeger has no traces after ~05:26:19 in this target (payment search 05:25-05:57 returned spans only to 05:26:19; checkout searches for 05:28-05:40 and 05:53-05:57 returned no traces), so the failing 05:32-05:37 spans, their gRPC status codes and their parent-child edges cannot be inspected directly.

Pod logs end early: payment read through 05:44:51.957, checkout 05:44:53.588, frontend-proxy 05:44:55.867, and the frontend container produced no readable log lines in 05:28-05:40; behaviour between ~05:45 and 05:57 is therefore not covered by logs.
The previous payment pod (payment-55766d76b9-846r8) and its container logs no longer exist, so payment's state and behaviour before 05:30:57 could not be inspected.
rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count had no rpc_service label values in this window (query returned nothing), so gRPC status codes such as UNAVAILABLE could not be confirmed from that metric.
No CPU throttling or container resource metric was found, so the hypothesis that the 20m CPU limit slowed payment's startup is unverified.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate Prometheus/Alertmanager rule (expression, for-duration, threshold) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration source that owns it, since it is not loaded in this scrape target.
Consult the change/audit trail for otel-demo/payment (rollout restart at 05:30:54Z) and otel-demo/flagd (restart at 05:00:36Z) to establish what prompted them and whether flagd-config was edited.
Add a readinessProbe/startupProbe to the payment container and evaluate raising its CPU limit, then re-test a payment-only rollout to confirm checkout Charge calls no longer fail.
Verify the fault-injection policy: decide whether 'paymentUnreachable' should remain 'on' in otel-demo/flagd-config.
Once Jaeger retains traces for 05:32-05:37, confirm the checkout -> payment Charge error status (for example UNAVAILABLE/connection refused) on an actual trace.
